هذا المستند يبين
 خطوات استبدال اسطوانات 
Co2 
عند اختبار النظام أو عمل نظام الأطفاء الذاتى للوحدة الغازية

يتكون نظام الاطفاء الذاتى بغاز 
 CO2 من عدد من الاسطوانات يوجد بداخلها غاز ثانى اكسيد 
 الكربون فى حالته السائلة تحت ضغط 80 بار تقريبا كما يتم وضع هذه الاسطوانات فى 
 مجموعات طبقا لكمية الغاز المطلوبة للاطفاء وتكون كل مجموعة من هذه المجموعات 
 مخصصة لاطفاء الحريق فى منطقة محددة تتناسب مع حجم الغاز داخل هذه الاسطوانات 
 ويوجد رشاشات لغاز الاطفاء ومكتشفات لهب موزعة كما بالجدول التالى:-

وكل من مكتشفات اللهب 
والحرارة لها خطين غير معتمدين على بعضهما ولكى يعمل نظام الحريق لا بد ان تاتى 
اشارة انذار بوجود حريق من احد مكتشفات الحريق على الخط الاول 
مقترنة بانذار على 
احد مكتشفات الحريق على الخط الثانى فان سولونيد تحرير الاوزان يتحرق فيعمل نظام 
الحريق وفى نفس الوقت تذهب اشارة الخروج الاضطرارى 
Trip من مفتاح
limit switch الى مختلف مكونات الوحدة لكى تتوقف ويعمل 
نظام الحركة البطيئة 
وفى حالة اشتغال نظام الاطفاء الذاتى يحدث تفريغ للاسطوانات وفى هذه الحالة يتم 
استبدالها

تم اعداد 
هذا المستند بواسطة السيد المهندس / يسرى عبد الحليم عبد اللطيف واختبره السيد المهندس / وصفى 
وليم ناشد - كبير مهندسين ادارة السلامة والصحة المهنية 
ووافق عليه السيد المهندس / محمد محمد اللاوندى المدير العام وتمت المراجعة من السيد الكيميائى / احمد السيد ابراهيم 
والسيد المهندس / سليمان زكى سليمان مدير عام ضمان وتأكيد الجودة وتم اعتماده من السيد المهندس / محمد محمد فرج عنان - رئيس قطاع محطة 
توليد كهرباء دمياط 
والسيد 
المهندس/ 
محمد حسين جمعه رئيس قطاع

rows:
وضع الاسطوانة عند حامل الاسطوانات 
 عند موضع تركيبها

فك غطاء الحماية 
 A ووضعة فى مكان 
 آمن لحين اعادة استخدامة 
 مع ملاحظة عدم جذب تيلة الامان لبلف الاسطوانة

ربط اذرع التعليق 
 B فى رأس الاسطوانة

وضع رافعة الاسطوانات 
 C اسفل الاسطوانة ورفع الاسطوانة لأعلى حتى 
 يمكن تثبيت اذرع التعليق B فى جهاز 
 الوزن D الحامل للاسطوانة مع التأكد 
 من ان الاسطوانة تم تركيبها فى وضع اتجاه الفتح الصحيح للبلف 
 حيث ان بلف الاسطوانة له اتجاه معين للفتح

رفع السدادة من على فتحة بلف الاسطوانة وتركيب خرطوم الضغط 
 العالى 
 E فى بلف الاسطوانة مع ملاحظة وضع جوان من 
 الجرنجريت لاحكام الربط

Damietta Combined Cycle Power Station

Procedure:
Replacing the CO2 cylinders when testing the system or when the automatic fire extinguishing system operates

sections_en.text: This document explains the steps for replacing the CO2 cylinders when testing the system or when the automatic fire extinguishing system of the gas unit operates.

The CO2 automatic fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state at a pressure of approximately 80 bar. These cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area commensurate with the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas sprinklers and flame detectors distributed as in the following table:-

Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate, a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line; then the weight-release solenoid moves and the fire system operates. At the same time, the emergency trip signal goes from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop, and the slow turning system operates. When the automatic fire extinguishing system operates, the cylinders are discharged, and in this case they are replaced.

This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif and tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed - Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department - and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed El-Lawandy, General Manager. It was reviewed by Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan - Head of the Damietta Power Generation Station Sector - and Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of the Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector at the East Delta Electricity Production Company.

rows: Place the cylinder on the cylinder holder at its installation position
Remove protection cover A and place it in a safe place until it is reused, taking care not to pull the safety pin of the cylinder valve
Fasten suspension arms B to the cylinder head

Place cylinder hoist C under the cylinder and raise the cylinder up so that suspension arms B can be fixed in weighing device D, which carries the cylinder, making sure that the cylinder is installed in the correct valve opening direction, since the cylinder valve has a specific opening direction
Remove the plug from the cylinder valve opening and fit the high pressure hose E into the cylinder valve, taking care to place a Klingerit gasket to ensure a tight connection

Introduction
This document explains the steps for replacing the CO2 cylinders when testing the system or when the automatic fire extinguishing system of the gas unit operates.
The CO2 automatic fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state at a pressure of approximately 80 bar. These cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area commensurate with the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas sprinklers and flame detectors distributed as in the following table:-
Flame detector | Heat detector | Sprinklers | Number of cylinders | 
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Right combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Left combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 8 | 7 | Oil tank
Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate, a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line; then the weight-release solenoid moves and the fire system operates. At the same time, the emergency trip signal goes from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop, and the slow turning system operates. When the automatic fire extinguishing system operates, the cylinders are discharged, and in this case they are replaced.
This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif and tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed - Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department - and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed El-Lawandy, General Manager. It was reviewed by Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan - Head of the Damietta Power Generation Station Sector - and Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of the Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector at the East Delta Electricity Production Company.
Safety precautions
Open the work order | 
Wear personal protective equipment | 
Tools, instruments and equipment used
 | Cylinder hoist | 
Wrench No. (28-30) | 
Adjustable wrench | 
Pliers | 
Procedures to be carried out
Place the cylinder on the cylinder holder at its installation position | 1.
Remove protection cover A and place it in a safe place until it is reused, taking care not to pull the safety pin of the cylinder valve | 2.
Fasten suspension arms B to the cylinder head | 3
Place cylinder hoist C under the cylinder and raise the cylinder up so that suspension arms B can be fixed in weighing device D, which carries the cylinder, making sure that the cylinder is installed in the correct valve opening direction, since the cylinder valve has a specific opening direction | 4.
Remove the plug from the cylinder valve opening and fit the high pressure hose E into the cylinder valve, taking care to place a Klingerit gasket to ensure a tight connection | 5.
